front: Define post hoc ergo propter hoc.
why: Post hoc is the correlation/causation flaw, the most common tested reasoning error

front: How do you recognize a straw man in a passage?
why: Straw-man recognition is occasionally the point of a critique question
False-dichotomy pattern appears occasionally in reasoning-flaw questions
Hasty generalization is the sample-scope flaw tested frequently

front: What is a slippery slope fallacy?
why: Slippery slope is a recognizable but infrequent CARS pattern

front: What is an ad hominem fallacy?
why: Ad hominem rarely appears in academic CARS prose; name-only trivia

front: What is an appeal to authority fallacy?
why: Appeal to authority surfaces when passages cite experts; secondary

front: What is an appeal to ignorance?
why: Appeal to ignorance is seldom the flaw a CARS question targets
Equivocation ties to word-in-context shifts; useful but niche
